To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Community Land Model is sensitive to a number of hydrologic parameters and that this sensitivity varies by site and climate regime.
the sensitivity of surface flux simulations is highly dependent on the hydrologic regime of a study site.

the Community Land Model version 4 (CLM4.5) simulated latent and sensible heat fluxes have the largest sensitivity to parameters related to subsurface runoff and vadose zone soil moisture processes for most of the study sites, while the sensitivity of the model outputs to parameters related to surface runoff and soil moisture processes are also important for sites with deep root vegetation and fine soil texture.

the development of an uncertainty quantification methodology for hydrologic parameters in a land surface model.
the sensitivity of surface flux simulations of CLM4 to selected hydrologic model parameters, using the UQ framework.
